paragraphs.title: Jehoshaphat’s Alliance with Ahab and the Call to War

easy.q: With whom did Jehoshaphat join affinity?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat went down to Ahab at Samaria.
easy.q: Where did Jehoshaphat go to visit Ahab?

answers: Go up to battle at Ramoth-gilead
easy.explanation: Ahab persuaded Jehoshaphat to go with him to Ramoth-gilead.
easy.q: What did Ahab persuade Jehoshaphat to do?

answers: To know whether they should go to battle
medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat wanted to hear the LORD’s word before going to war.
medium.q: Why did Jehoshaphat ask to enquire at the word of the LORD?

medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat joined affinity with Ahab and became related to him.
medium.q: What relationship between Jehoshaphat and Ahab is described at the beginning?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes a great supply of sheep and oxen prepared for the guests.
medium.q: What does the phrase “Ahab killed sheep and oxen for him in abundance” indicate?

answers: He agreed to cooperate in the war
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat expressed his willingness to join Ahab and his army.
challenge.q: What does Jehoshaphat’s answer, “I am as thou art,” show?

answers: He agrees to war but first asks for the LORD’s word
He refuses to meet Ahab but goes to war
He asks for a prophet but rejects the proposal
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat agrees to the campaign but insists on seeking God’s guidance first.
challenge.q: What is the main tension in Jehoshaphat’s actions?

answers: The battle, the alliance, the feast, and the prophetic inquiry
The alliance, the visit to Samaria, the proposal for war, and the request to enquire of the LORD
The request to enquire of the LORD, the alliance, the visit, and the feast
challenge.explanation: This is the order presented in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is correct?

paragraphs.title: Ahab’s Prophets and the Arrival of Micaiah

easy.explanation: The king gathered four hundred prophets.
easy.q: How many prophets did the king of Israel gather?

easy.explanation: They told Ahab to go up to Ramoth-gilead.
easy.q: What did the prophets tell Ahab?

easy.explanation: Ahab identified Micaiah the son of Imla as the other prophet.
easy.q: Which additional prophet did Jehoshaphat ask to consult?

answers: He wanted to hear the word of the LORD also
There were no prophets in Samaria
He wanted to appoint a captain
medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked whether there was another prophet of the LORD to consult.
medium.q: Why did Jehoshaphat ask for another prophet?

answers: Micaiah would not come to Samaria
Micaiah never prophesied good concerning him
medium.explanation: Ahab said that Micaiah always prophesied evil concerning him.
The king ordered one of his officers to fetch Micaiah quickly.
medium.q: What was the messenger instructed to do?

answers: He wanted their message tested by another prophet
He knew they were not prophets
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat was not satisfied without hearing another prophet of the LORD.
challenge.q: What does Jehoshaphat’s request reveal about his response to the four hundred prophets?

answers: Speak like the other prophets and prophesy good
challenge.explanation: The messenger asked Micaiah to agree with the other prophets and speak good.
challenge.q: What did the messenger ask Micaiah to do?

answers: He refused to speak at all
He would speak only what God said
He would speak only to Jehoshaphat
challenge.explanation: Micaiah declared that he would speak what his God said.
challenge.q: What distinguished Micaiah from the messenger and the other prophets?

easy.explanation: Micaiah first said, “Go ye up, and prosper.”
easy.q: What did Micaiah first say when asked whether they should go to battle?

answers: As sheep that have no shepherd
easy.explanation: He saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains as sheep without a shepherd.
easy.q: How did Micaiah describe Israel in his vision?

easy.explanation: He saw all the host of heaven standing on the LORD’s right and left.
easy.q: What did Micaiah see before the LORD’s throne?

answers: The king required him to speak the truth in the LORD’s name
medium.explanation: Ahab adjured Micaiah to speak nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD.
medium.q: Why did Micaiah change from his first words?

answers: Israel will be without a leader
Israel will live only in the mountains
medium.explanation: The image points to Israel being scattered and without a master.
medium.q: What does the image of sheep without a shepherd suggest?

answers: A spirit that causes the prophets to speak falsely
A strong wind from the mountains
medium.explanation: The lying spirit was placed in the mouths of Ahab’s prophets.
medium.q: What is the “lying spirit” in Micaiah’s vision?

answers: Ahab’s fall will leave Israel scattered and without a leader
Ahab will appoint a new shepherd
Israel will lead Ahab to victory
challenge.explanation: The vision portrays the result of the king’s downfall and Israel’s scattering.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the scattered sheep and Ahab’s fate?

answers: A lying spirit is in their mouths
They do not know about the battle
challenge.explanation: Micaiah says that the LORD has put a lying spirit in their mouths.
challenge.q: How does Micaiah explain why all the other prophets promise success?

answers: He sounds like the other prophets but later reveals the truth
He prophesies victory only for Jehoshaphat
He refuses to speak to the king
challenge.explanation: His first words repeat the prophets’ message, but his later vision exposes its falsehood.
challenge.q: What is ironic about Micaiah’s first words?

paragraphs.title: Confrontation with Zedekiah and Micaiah’s Imprisonment

easy.explanation: Zedekiah struck Micaiah upon the cheek.
easy.q: Who struck Micaiah on the cheek?

easy.explanation: Ahab ordered that Micaiah be carried back to prison.
easy.q: Where did Ahab order Micaiah to be taken?

easy.explanation: Ahab ordered that Micaiah be fed with bread and water of affliction.
easy.q: What was Micaiah to be given in prison?

answers: How the Spirit of the LORD had gone from him to speak to Micaiah
medium.explanation: Zedekiah asked which way the Spirit of the LORD had gone from him to Micaiah.
medium.q: What did Zedekiah challenge Micaiah about?

answers: The day of defeat when he would hide in an inner chamber
That he would lead the army to victory
medium.explanation: Micaiah said Zedekiah would see that day and hide himself.
medium.q: What did Micaiah say Zedekiah would see?

answers: Meager food under harsh prison conditions
medium.explanation: The phrase describes restricted and difficult prison provisions.
medium.q: What does “bread of affliction and water of affliction” mean?

answers: He immediately takes back his prophecy
He stands by his message and calls the people to hear
challenge.explanation: Micaiah remains firm and says, “Hearken, all ye people.”
challenge.q: What does Micaiah’s response show about him under pressure?

answers: Micaiah’s prophecy opposed what the king wanted to hear
challenge.explanation: Ahab punished Micaiah after hearing his prophecy of judgment.
challenge.q: Why did Ahab order Micaiah to be imprisoned?

answers: If Ahab returned in peace, the LORD had not spoken by him
If Zedekiah apologized, the prophecy would come true
If Jehoshaphat won, Micaiah would become king
challenge.explanation: Micaiah said that Ahab’s peaceful return would prove the LORD had not spoken through him.
challenge.q: What condition did Micaiah give for testing his prophecy?

easy.explanation: The two kings went up to Ramoth-gilead.
easy.q: Where did Ahab and Jehoshaphat go up to fight?

easy.explanation: Ahab disguised himself before entering the battle.
easy.q: Who disguised himself in the battle?

easy.explanation: The king of Syria commanded them to fight only with the king of Israel.
easy.q: Whom were the captains of the chariots commanded to fight?

answers: They thought he was the king of Israel
He was disguised as the king of Syria
medium.explanation: When they saw Jehoshaphat, they mistakenly thought he was Ahab.
medium.q: Why did the chariot captains first pursue Jehoshaphat?

answers: He cried out, and the LORD helped him
He surrendered to the king of Syria
medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat cried out, and God moved the captains away from him.
medium.q: What did Jehoshaphat do when the chariot captains surrounded him?

medium.explanation: Ahab changed his appearance so that the enemy would not recognize him.
medium.q: What does it mean that Ahab “disguised” himself?

answers: Ahab hid his identity while Jehoshaphat wore his royal robes
Jehoshaphat wore the king of Syria’s clothing
challenge.explanation: Ahab disguised himself, but Jehoshaphat wore his royal clothing.
challenge.q: What difference was there between Ahab’s clothing and Jehoshaphat’s?

answers: It shifted to Jehoshaphat and then was removed from him
It shifted from Syria’s king to the prophets
challenge.explanation: The captains pursued Jehoshaphat, but the LORD caused them to turn away.
challenge.q: How did the danger change during the battle?

answers: The LORD helped him when he cried out
Jehoshaphat was saved because he disguised himself
challenge.explanation: The passage directly attributes Jehoshaphat’s rescue to the LORD’s help.

easy.explanation: A certain man drew a bow, and an arrow struck Ahab.

answers: Between the joints of the harness
easy.explanation: The arrow struck Ahab between the joints of the harness.
easy.q: Where did the arrow strike Ahab?

answers: About the time of the sun going down
easy.explanation: Ahab died about the time of the sun going down.

answers: He wanted to speak with Micaiah
medium.explanation: Ahab told his chariot man that he was wounded.
medium.q: Why did Ahab ask to be carried out of the battle?

medium.explanation: Ahab stayed himself up in his chariot until the even.
medium.q: How long did Ahab remain in his chariot against the Syrians?

answers: Knowing that he would strike the king
medium.explanation: The man drew his bow without intentionally targeting Ahab.
medium.q: What does “at a venture” mean in the phrase describing the archer?

answers: Ahab’s wounding and death fulfill the warning of judgment
The wound saves Ahab from the battle
The wound proves Ahab’s prophets were right
challenge.explanation: Ahab was wounded and died in battle, confirming Micaiah’s prophecy.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the arrow and Micaiah’s prophecy?

answers: He remained despite his wound rather than weakening the army’s resolve
challenge.explanation: Ahab continued in the battle even after being wounded.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Ahab’s remaining in the battle until evening?

answers: He was wounded, remained in battle until evening, and died at sunset
He disguised himself, won, and returned to Samaria
He was wounded in the morning and healed by evening
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence given in the final verses.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Ahab’s death?
